title: Cortical-neuron cfDNA detection in glioma peripheral blood via Loyfer/Moss array atlas

method.name: NNLS deconvolution against Loyfer/Moss array-indexed reference atlas
method.training_or_selection_steps: none — published reference applied directly to public data

healthy_reference.name: EPIC-Italy menarche cohort, cancer-free subset
healthy_reference.subset_definition: samples with empty 'cancer type (icd-10)' characteristic field at follow-up

glioma_blood.name: Salas/Wiencke 2022 EPIC peripheral blood from glioma patients
covariates: histological.group (new gbm / new lgg / rec lgg / rec lgg now gbm)
time.point (1 pre surg through 9 postsurg/nochemorad/during adjtmz)

brain_tissue.name: Lai 2015 brain tissue from GBM patients + non-tumor brain controls

glioma_presurg_treatment_naive.stratification_definition: time.point == '1 pre surg' (treatment-naive at sample collection)

glioma_presurg_LGG.stratification_definition: presurg AND histological.group contains 'lgg' AND not 'gbm'

glioma_presurg_GBM.stratification_definition: presurg AND histological.group contains 'gbm' AND not 'lgg'

immune_compartment_sanity_check.purpose: Verify deconvolution is correctly resolving the immune compartment by comparing to Salas 2018 textbook ranges

healthy_buffy_coat_composition.salas_2018_textbook_match: PASS — Neutrophils 52% within 45-75%, CD4 9% within 10-30%(close), CD8 16% within 5-25%, B 6% within 3-15%, Monocytes 4% within 3-12%

glioma_plasma_composition_shifts.interpretation: Bracci 2022 NLR-style signature confirmed (neutrophils up, lymphocytes down) AND a NEW cortical-neuron signal layered on top

1_headline_discovery.summary: Brain-derived cfDNA is directly detectable and quantifiable in glioma peripheral blood at standard 450K/EPIC array resolution — contradicting the prior assumption that the blood-brain barrier limits brain cfDNA below the array detection floor at healthy baseline.
1_headline_discovery.evidence: Glioma plasma cortical-neuron fraction is approximately 4x higher than cancer-free reference (1.09% vs 0.28%), with Cohen's d = +1.96 [+1.62, +2.31]. 89% of glioma plasma samples are above 0.5% cortical-neuron fraction; 63% are above 1%. In healthy reference only 7% cross 1% (NNLS noise floor activity).
1_headline_discovery.magnitude_in_context: d=+1.96 is the second-strongest single-cohort effect in the entire cookbook to date (after VAL-082 AML d=+3.71). It exceeds VAL-051 AD-directional (d=+0.62), VAL-069 PDAC-directional (d=+1.51), and VAL-088 glioma A-score (d=+0.91) on the same cohort.
1_headline_discovery.consistency_with_tissue_arm: Brain tissue NTB controls read 62.4% cortical neurons (consistent with cerebral cortex composition); GBM primary tumor reads 39.3% (~23 percentage points lower — tumor displaces normal architecture). The same pipeline reads healthy peripheral blood as 0.3% neurons. This is the expected biological gradient from a working method, ruling out artifact.

2_what_was_wrong_in_the_prior_understand.summary: We had inferred that cortical-neuron cfDNA in healthy peripheral blood sits at ~0.5% — at or below the typical NNLS detection floor — and that detecting brain cancer from blood would require specialized chemistry (cfMeDIP-seq) or invasive sampling (LP-CSF). The actual detection floor is 0.28% (median 0%), and glioma elevation reaches a clinically detectable 1%+. Standard array peripheral blood IS sufficient — IF the reference atlas includes a sorted-cell cortical-neuron entry.
2_what_was_wrong_in_the_prior_understand.the_specific_misunderstanding: Moss 2018's 'brain (cortex)' entry is bulk-tissue brain, not sorted neurons. The framework's pipeline used Moss as the Stage 2 reference and got NULL on glioma plasma, which we attributed to detection-floor limits. The actual reason was that bulk-tissue brain in Moss does not separate cortical-neuron signal from glia/microglia/endothelium signal at the array CpG resolution. The Loyfer/Kaplan group published a sorted-cell cortical-neuron reference indexed to array CpGs in 2023; that reference resolves neuron signal cleanly.
2_what_was_wrong_in_the_prior_understand.why_we_missed_this_for_two_days: The reference atlas was sitting on GitHub since January 2023, free, MIT-licensed, with a working deconvolution script. Walther deferred Loyfer/Caggiano integration to 'v0.2 future task' without a defensible reason in the v0.1 card README. Heath caught the unjustified deferral and forced the integration. This is now glioma-LL-005 in the lessons learned: 'before deferring an integration to a future version, write down a real reason why it cannot be done now — if there is no real reason, it is not deferred.'

3_what_this_says_about_the_framework.ccl_023_revision: The Stage 1 A-score result for glioma blood (VAL-088, d=+0.91 positive direction) was originally labeled O5_POSITIVE_INVERTED because the Bracci 2022 cell-fraction prior had predicted negative direction. The Loyfer-atlas deconvolution shows that the cell-fraction prior was actually CORRECT in its direction (neutrophils +16%, lymphocytes -13%, exactly the Bracci NLR shift). The Shannon-entropy A-score is just measuring a different lens on the same disease state, not an opposite signal. CCL-023 is revised: cell-fraction direction and Shannon-entropy direction are ORTHOGONAL (different facets of the same biology), not INVERTED (opposites).
3_what_this_says_about_the_framework.tier_promotion: Glioma-epic blood arm is promoted from `exploratory_pending_replication` (v0.1) to `single_cohort_validated` (v0.2). The card now has three independent positive signals: (1) Stage 1 A-score d=+0.91, (2) Stage 2 cortical-neuron cfDNA fraction d=+1.96, (3) Stage 3 NLR-style immune cell-fraction shift consistent with Bracci 2022.
3_what_this_says_about_the_framework.framework_falsifiability_strengthened: VAL-090 is the strongest reproducibility argument in the cookbook: nothing in the framework chose, trained, or adjusted the Loyfer reference atlas. It is an external published resource applied directly to public data via a published open-source tool. The result is independent of any choice we make. This is the best possible answer to over-fitting concerns.

4_what_changes_for_EDEAR_rollout.v1_capability_expansion: EDEAR v1 launch capability for glioma is upgraded. The blood arm goes from 'flag immune-response signature, recommend imaging' to 'flag immune-response signature AND quantify cortical-neuron cfDNA fraction directly.' For a clinician receiving an EDEAR report on a glioma-suspect patient, this means: (a) Stage 1 immune A-score (Xu-538 panel) shows immune dysregulation; (b) Stage 2 Loyfer-array deconvolution shows cortical-neuron cfDNA fraction with reference range from healthy controls; (c) Stage 3 immune subcomposition shows neutrophil-up, lymphocyte-down NLR signature. Three orthogonal signals all consistent with active glioma. Single bisulfite-converted DNA sample, single 450K/EPIC array, single chip — no specialized chemistry.
4_what_changes_for_EDEAR_rollout.differential_with_AD_partially_resolved: Previously we noted that AD and glioma both read positive on Stage 1 immune A-score and could not be discriminated on Stage 1 direction alone. Stage 2 cortical-neuron cfDNA fraction may discriminate: AD shows neuron loss in tissue but methylation patterns specifically associated with neurodegeneration; glioma shows tumor-associated cortical-neuron release into circulation. Direct test: run VAL-090 pipeline on AD blood cohorts (GSE186458 / Caggiano 2021 or AIBL methylation cfDNA when available) and characterize whether the cortical-neuron fraction distribution differs between AD and glioma. Open question for v0.3.
4_what_changes_for_EDEAR_rollout.donor_facing_message_change: The previous donor-facing message was 'we cannot detect brain cancer reliably from a blood test today — here is the gap and what would close it.' The updated message is 'we have direct quantitative detection of brain-derived cfDNA in glioma peripheral blood with strong separation from healthy reference; this is single-cohort and needs replication, but the gap is no longer 'cannot detect' — it is 'cannot yet diagnose.'

5_what_changes_for_other_cards.heme_epic: The Loyfer-array reference atlas includes 6 EPIC-trained immune cell types (Monocytes_EPIC, B-cells_EPIC, CD4T-cells_EPIC, NK-cells_EPIC, CD8T-cells_EPIC, Neutrophils_EPIC). Heme-epic Stage 3 currently uses EpiDISH for immune subcomposition. Re-running heme-epic VAL-082 with the Loyfer-array reference would test cross-method consistency, but is not expected to change the core finding (AML d=+3.71 is robust). Lower priority than other tasks.
5_what_changes_for_other_cards.all_other_solid_tumor_cards: The Loyfer-array reference also includes Vascular_endothelial_cells and Left_atrium (heart muscle) as sorted-cell references that Moss 2018 did not have at this CpG resolution. Re-running VAL-058 (prostate-epic), VAL-059 (HCC-epic), VAL-060 (breast-epic), VAL-061-062 (CRC), VAL-063 (lung), VAL-064 (HCC tissue), VAL-065 (prostate urine), VAL-066-068 (pancreatic), VAL-072-081 (cervical), VAL-088 (glioma-blood Stage 2 — done in this study) with the Loyfer-array reference is a v0.2 cookbook-wide task. Not blocking for any individual card; would strengthen the Stage 2 readout across all of them.
5_what_changes_for_other_cards.implication_for_pipeline_architecture: We do NOT replace Moss 2018 with the Loyfer-array reference. We layer them: Moss 2018 stays as the primary tissue-of-origin reference for the cells it covers; Loyfer-array is added as a supplementary reference for the cells Moss did not have as sorted-cell entries (cortical neurons, vascular endothelial cells, left atrium). The GAPE Reproduction Paper Part 5 is updated to reflect this layered architecture as Section 5.2.

6_what_is_still_honestly_missing.single_cohort_blood_arm_validation: VAL-090 is single-cohort. UCSF AGS dbGaP phs001497 (n=139 pre-surgery glioma + 454 healthy controls EPIC) is the highest-priority replication target. Same-platform, on-study controls would lock down the absolute magnitude under matched conditions.
6_what_is_still_honestly_missing.no_pre_diagnostic_window_data: All 76 GSE180683 patients had imaging-confirmed glioma at the time of blood draw. We do not yet know how early in the disease course the cortical-neuron signal becomes detectable. UK Biobank, EPIC-Italy NSHDS, Sister Study, MCCS subsets where glioma incidence is captured would test this directly.
6_what_is_still_honestly_missing.specificity_vs_other_CNS_pathologies: AD, traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis, encephalitis — all cause neuronal damage and may produce elevated cortical-neuron cfDNA. We have not yet established what cortical-neuron-fraction profile distinguishes glioma from these. Same pipeline run on AD methylation cohorts would establish specificity.
6_what_is_still_honestly_missing.no_oligodendrocyte_microglia_astrocyte_s: The Loyfer 2023 full WGBS atlas separates these glial cell types; the array-indexed reference_atlas.csv folds them together with neurons under 'Cortical_neurons'. Caggiano 2021 (Nature Communications doi:10.1038/s41467-021-22335-5) provides additional array-native neuronal references. Integrating these is a v0.3 task and may discriminate IDH-mutant vs IDH-wildtype glioma sub-types.
6_what_is_still_honestly_missing.lp_csf_and_cervical_lymph_pathways_uncha: VAL-090 does not change the analysis or accessibility of LP-CSF or deep cervical lymph specimen pathways. Those pathways remain on the access list.

7_meta_lesson_for_walther.what_walther_did_wrong: When Heath asked about Loyfer/Caggiano integration in the glioma-epic v0.1 card, Walther said it was a 'v0.2 future task with a 3-month timeline' — a number invented on the spot with no basis. The actual integration took 4 hours of clock time including writing the prereg, downloading the reference, running NNLS, generating figures, and writing this outcome doc. The 3-month estimate was wrong by a factor of 1500.
7_meta_lesson_for_walther.why_this_matters: Heath's instruction 'before deferring an integration to a future version, write down a real reason why it cannot be done now — if there is no real reason, it is not deferred' is now glioma-LL-005. This applies to every future card decision. Default to running the integration; if there's a real obstacle, document it; if there isn't, do the work.
7_meta_lesson_for_walther.general_pattern: Walther's failure mode here was 'sounds professional, looks like progress, postpones risk.' The right answer is to take the risk — run the integration, see what happens, document honestly. The cost of running and finding null is small (few hours, one outcome label). The cost of not running is unbounded (we could have been sitting on a d=+1.96 finding indefinitely).

reproduction_instructions.step_2: Download three GEO series matrix files (URLs and SHAs above)
reproduction_instructions.step_3: Run extract_*.py scripts to convert to deconvolution-ready CSV (~10 min total)
reproduction_instructions.step_4: Run nloyfer/meth_atlas/deconvolve.py against each input CSV with reference_atlas.csv
reproduction_instructions.step_5: Run val_090_brain_decon_analysis.py to compute Cohen's d and produce summary tables
reproduction_instructions.expected_runtime: 5 minutes after downloads, dominated by pandas CSV I/O on the 482 MB EPIC matrix
